old: A phase 2 study evaluated the safety and immunogenicity of two investigational mRNA vaccines against SARS-CoV-2, compared to a licensed bivalent vaccine. Both investigational vaccines showed dose-dependent increases in neutralizing antibodies and T-cell responses, with an acceptable safety profile. However, the small sample size and lack of formal hypothesis testing limit the ability to draw definitive conclusions about their comparative efficacy.
new: This phase 2 randomized trial compared investigational COVID-19 mRNA boosters with a licensed vaccine in previously vaccinated adults. The bivalent CV0701 vaccine produced dose-dependent neutralizing-antibody responses, and no vaccine-related serious adverse events were reported. The small study assessed safety and immune responses, so it could not establish clinical protection or reliably detect rare harms.
basis: Full-text design, safety and limitations; CV0601 had only one dose level
